text:
Ash Lee: Quick sync — following the RFC fallout, we need a small plan for minimizing cross-service deps from edge SDKs to ingest while preserving cost attribution
Ravi Patel: +1. current problem: every sdk sends full attribution envelope, blowup in payload size and metadata churn
Sofia Morales: We discussed a compact-ref approach in the RFC: send a tiny attr_ref instead of full attrs and let ingest resolve. that reduces wire by ~60% for high-traffic mobile events
Matt Garcia: Concern: late-resolve means backfills and queries need resolution service. That's extra operational surface and a potential availability hotspot
Jin Wang: proposed compromise: keep attr_ref + occasionally sample full attrs (1%) to allow rebuilds without relying solely on resolution service
Ravi Patel: sampling helps but doesn't fix real-time cost attribution for billing flows. what if we provide two handshake modes: "adhoc" (full attrs) and "deferred" (attr_ref) and routing decides per-tenant based on commit tier
Ash Lee: I like per-tenant handshake. Could be configured at SDK init or via server flag. default=deferred for free tier, adhoc for enterprise. keeps payload small for most customers
Sofia Morales: Operational notes: resolution service needs to be idempotent and store mapping with TTL. suggest key:</> `attr_ref:{tenant}:{hash}` and a small proto with {timestamp, version, payload_s3_path?}
Matt Garcia: If we store payload in S3 or object store, we avoid large DB writes. But then we need consistent lifecycle (delete after X days) and a cheap lookup cache for hot refs
Jin Wang: caching layer (LRU) + local shard map per ingest region should work. add health-check endpoints and fallback — if resolve fails, mark event as "attr-missing" and route to degraded billing pipeline
Ravi Patel: Edge-case: SDKs behind flaky networks may never send full attrs, causing attr_ref to point to missing payload. we should accept a short inline fallback: up to 1kb of inline attrs when network heuristics suggest retry/backoff
Ash Lee: Implementation checklist:
- add handshake config to SDKs + server flag (Ash)
- small attr resolution service proto + S3 artifact flow (Jin)
- sample-full-attrs job + replay test harness (Sofia)
- billing pipeline changes to accept unresolved markers and run async join (Ravi)
- metrics: percent deferred, resolve latency, missing-attr-rate (all)
Sofia Morales: quick example header we can use in SDKs:
```http
X-Redwood-Attr-Ref: attr_ref:acct_123:sha1_abcdef012345
X-Redwood-Attr-Mode: deferred
```
Matt Garcia: QA: add test where resolution service is disabled and assert billing doesn't lose revenue (expect queued/async fallback)
Jin Wang: Also consider a migration window: start by offering attr_ref as opt-in for 2 weeks, then flip default for new SDK versions after we validate metrics
Ash Lee: Cool. I'll open tickets with the checklist and we can pair on the proto. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
ingest-bot: deploy-check successful for branch "attr-ref-proto" — no conflicts
Ravi Patel: small follow-up — one more tradeoff: schema evolution. if attr schema changes, attr_ref blobs must be versioned and resolution must be able to transform old->new for billing logic
Sofia Morales: agree. add version header in proto and a migration util in the resolver. also add an eval metric for billing delta post-migration
Ash Lee: OK tickets created, linking here: https://redwood.example/boards/INFR/attrs-ref-epic (I'll add assignees). Meeting in 30m for proto sketch
Matt Garcia: bringing diagrams, will sketch flow where resolve cache is a sidecar to ingest nodes
Jin Wang: if time runs short, we can do a strawman PR for the proto today and iterate
Ash Lee: Thanks — wrapping up.
